title: The head objective axis: penalty ladder below 1.0, smoothed targets, and a batch-hinge margin objective on the sealed 6144-atom codes
question: Accuracy lives in the thin positive-margin tail (M128). Does the frozen-code accuracy depend on the head OBJECTIVE - under-regularised ridge (lambda < 1.0, never measured; lambda >= 1.0 is sealed at M108 and declines), smoothed targets (registered analytic expectation: predictions identical to lambda=1.0 ridge), or a true margin objective (batch multi-class hinge)?

sealed_codes.note: Reuses the SEALED M117 6144-atom code memmaps (data_cache_root()/v16/m117). No re-encode, no GPU, CPU-only.

ridge.note: One streaming Gram; solve_many. lambda >= 1.0 already sealed at M108 (monotone decline); lambda < 1.0 is the unmeasured direction.

smoothed.analytic_note: For a standardised ridge with intercept, Y_s = (1-e)Y + e/345 implies cross_s = (1-e)*cross (the e/345 term cancels the centring exactly) and intercept_s = (1-e)*p_hat + e/345. Scores shift by a per-row constant, so argmax predictions are IDENTICAL to the lambda=1.0 ridge. The cell verifies the lemma numerically, it does not discover it.

hinge.intercept: class prior p_hat of the n=34500 cell, IDENTICAL to the ridge head's intercept, so the only registered difference between the arms is the objective
hinge.step_rule: batch multi-class hinge subgradient: G accumulates X at the true class and -X at the best wrong class for every violating row, averaged over rows; W = (1 - 1/t) * W + (1/(lambda*t)) * G; t = epoch index; corpus order, deterministic
hinge.compute_note: n=34500 is the registered compute ceiling (24576 x 345 weight matrix; full-data hinge is the escalation cell only).

same_cell_ridge.note: Fresh ridge fit at n=34500 for the same-cell control (t2 anchor vs sealed Q(6144,34500)).

gate.t1_reference: ridge lambda=1.0 at n=138000 reproduces M117 sealed Q(6144,138000) = 0.2248695652173913
gate.t2_reference: ridge lambda=1.0 at n=34500 reproduces M117 sealed Q(6144,34500) = 0.09057971014492754
gate.kill_switch_objective: fired if NEITHER any lambda<1.0 ridge cell NOR any hinge cell beats its own same-cell ridge by >= +0.003. If fired: the head-objective axis is CLOSED and lambda=1.0 ridge remains the head (negative sealed and reported). If any cell beats the margin: the objective is a measured lever and that head escalates to full data.
gate.margin_report: f_true - max_other quantiles (q25/q50/q75/q95) and positive-margin share on the test set, for the hinge arm and its same-cell ridge control.
